question: Will Francesca Hong win the 2026 Wisconsin Governor Democratic primary election?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the Democratic Primary for Governor of Wisconsin, scheduled to take place on August 11, 2026. Resolution will be based on the overall winner of the primary, including any potential second round or run-off.

If no 2026 Wisconsin Gubernatorial Democratic Primary takes place, this market will resolve to “Other.”

The resolution source for this market will be the first official announcement of the results from the Wisconsin Democratic Party; however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

evidence.excerpt: A new Marquette Law School Poll survey of Democratic primary voters finds Francesca Hong leading with 38%, followed by Mandela Barnes with 16%, David Crowley at 7%, and Joel Brennan and Kelda Roys at 2% each; 34% remain undecided. Including respondents who lean toward a candidate, Hong receives 46%, Barnes 21%, and Crowley 11%, with 14% undecided. The survey was conducted July 22–27, 2026, among 407 registered voters who said they would vote in the Democratic primary, including early absentee voters, with a margin of error of plus or minus 6.6 percentage points. In the previous July 8–16 survey, Hong had 26% and Barnes 15%.

A State Navigate poll released Tuesday found Hong at 44%, Crowley at 15%, Barnes at 14%, and Roys, Brennan and Sara Rodriguez at 4% each, with 13% undecided. The survey interviewed nearly 1,100 Wisconsinites July 23–26, after Rodriguez’s withdrawal and Crowley’s reentry, and reported a margin of error of plus or minus 3 points. The poll was sponsored by liberal groups UpNorthNews and Main Street Action.

Crowley reentered the governor’s race on July 18 with an endorsement from Gov. Tony Evers, who had previously declined to support a primary candidate. Rodriguez had ended her campaign the previous day amid financial turmoil. Barnes criticized Crowley’s return, while Brennan and Roys indicated they would continue competing.

Hong reported raising nearly $709,000 and spending around $433,000 during the first six months of 2026, ending June with around $411,000. Barnes raised around $840,000, spent just over $1.1 million, and ended June with about $204,000. Brennan ended the period with close to $360,000, and Roys had about $406,000.

Barnes, Brennan, Crowley, Hong and Roys participated in a televised debate on July 28, largely agreeing on raising taxes on millionaires and increasing public education funding. Crowley was the only candidate to say he would have signed the failed bipartisan budget-surplus compromise. The Democratic primary was scheduled for August 11, and more than 107,000 absentee ballots had already been returned as of Tuesday, according to Wisconsin Elections Commission data.

A Wisconsin judge ruled July 29 that voters who had already returned absentee ballots for the primary could not void them and request new ballots. More than 117,000 absentee ballots had been returned by Wednesday. Rodriguez’s name remained on the ballot, along with Missy Hughes, who had dropped out in June.

A $2.2 million television advertising campaign by the Republican Governors Association began airing July 16, describing Hong as too liberal for Wisconsin and highlighting her immigration positions. Several Democrats, including Hong’s rivals, argued that the ads were intended to increase her appeal among Democratic primary voters. Hong publicly thanked the association for highlighting her legislative proposals.
